title: Care aftercare packet - standard inserts (v1)
description: Standard inserts the trainee can switch on in the Care aftercare packet, plus the helpline tables that print with them. Shape only: validate_care_inserts.py enforces what a schema cannot (print order, crisis single-source, number format and freshness, dose-literal and metadata bans, the unit-wording rules, the wallet card's five-line budget). TEXT RULES for every string: plain language (target grade 6); no markup; no phone number outside a table row; no crisis number typed (crisis contacts are referenced by id from crisis_resources.json); no dose literals; and only approved placeholders: {{unitContact}} expands the complete purpose/phone/staffed-hours/noncrisis template from independently approved unit fields; {{unitName}}, {{unitPhone}}, {{unitPurpose}}, {{unitHours}} and {{callbackTeam}}, {{callbackPhone}}, {{callbackHours}}, {{callbackFallback}} are approved profile values; {{callWindow}} and {{callDeadline}} are labelled handwriting blanks, never application fields; {{crisis:<id>}} uses the governed crisis contact. A unit reference must never imply round-the-clock crisis coverage. All patient output requires a fresh independent exact-version authorization. RENDERING CONTRACT: page 1 is the intro insert, then the crisis block, then the `week` insert; resource pages follow; then the remaining inserts in array order. The crisis block is built from crisisCopy.heading, crisisCopy.note and each `crisis` line, where the line's official NAME, contact and availability come from crisis_resources.json and only `when` comes from this file. It is NOT the shared learner crisis block, which is addressed to clinicians. The wallet card is a SEPARATE, optional print, never a packet page: it is built from the top-level `card` object plus crisisCopy.cardHeading and the same `crisis` lines (official name and contact from crisis_resources.json). An insert prints its title, then any of body, bullets, groups, rows, table, tip and signoff in that order; layout is the renderer's job. Review-mode chrome (the review band, tick boxes, 'tick the ones you want to try') is renderer-owned and not in this file. A row label of "" is an unlabelled handwriting line.

crisisCopy.description: Patient-facing framing for the crisis block and wallet card. Contains no number: lines come from `crisis`.

crisis.description: Crisis lines, as references to resource ids in crisis_resources.json (the single source of truth for crisis numbers and their official names). Order is print order. `when` is the only patient-facing text this file adds to a line.

card.description: The wallet card: a separate, optional one-sided print, not a packet page. title heads the print; body is the cutting instruction; mineTitle heads the write-in panel, and each of rows is a labelled line to write on. Contains no number: the crisis lines come from `crisis`.

inserts.description: In print order. defaultOn is the state when a trainee starts a new packet; core inserts cannot be switched off.

paragraphs.description: One or more paragraphs separated by a blank line.

rowLabels.description: Handwriting rows. The label is printed; the line is left blank. "" is an unlabelled line.

tableRow.description: One helpline. number is the dial string only (keypad steps like 'press 1' go in 'what'). verifiedDate is the date the number and every fact in 'what' were last checked against `source` (plus any `alsoSources`, for a fact the main page lacks, such as hours); each is the operating organization's or a government page, never an aggregator. Neither is ever printed.
